question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(8,-3,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨7,-2,4⟩)\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩=0.$

current_example.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,2,-2)$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equation ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14147962/assets/0dae19b55048807f08f1377c62d9f0545e9164caeffbf06a8ee7ed752d21601c.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(4,8,2).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14147962/assets/203d7b478241105ea7c04da39c819c8ebe7503e402949c052af29ac8c8dbc3e9.svg)

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 2+6\cdot 4+4\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-2+24-16|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,6\,|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
